# sheepdog

The fleet **enforcer** marker — declaring it makes a repo the one that covers and maintains every repo
under an owner. Opt-in (a dedicated sheepdog repo declares it; **not** seeded by `--init`). It
standardizes the fleet coverage that used to be bespoke Claudinite infrastructure into a declaration.

Thin by design: prose + the config schema (the sheepdog pack entry's `config` = `{ owner, kind, exclude,
canonRepo, staleDays }`) + three cross-repo **sweeps**, each with the one agentless scheduled task that
runs it (the sweep is its `prework`; no workflow of its own) — plus one **manual lever**
that has no cadence and therefore does have a workflow:

| sweep | task | asks |
|---|---|---|
| [check-fleet-coverage.mjs](tasks/fleet-census/check-fleet-coverage.mjs) | [fleet-census](tasks/fleet-census/task.md) (daily) | is this repo a **member**? → adoption issues |
| [check-fleet-freshness.mjs](tasks/fleet-freshness/check-fleet-freshness.mjs) | [fleet-freshness](tasks/fleet-freshness/task.md) (weekly) | is a member **keeping up**? → drift issues |
| [aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs](tasks/fleet-usage/aggregate-fleet-usage.mjs) | [fleet-usage](tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) (daily) | what does the fleet **actually use**? → `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` |
| [force-fleet-baseline.mjs](fleet-baseline/force-fleet-baseline.mjs) + [follow-fleet-baseline.mjs](fleet-baseline/follow-fleet-baseline.mjs) | *(no task — the [fleet-baseline workflow](stubs/workflows/fleet-baseline.yml), `workflow_dispatch` only)* | make every member baseline **now**, watch each one finish → what the fleet did |

The second exists because per-project scheduling made every member maintain itself and, in doing so,
removed the last thing that looked at a member from the **outside** — self-maintenance cannot detect its
own absence. The third exists for the same shape of reason one rung up: a member can say whether a
skill loads *there*, and only a view across every member can say whether it earns its place at all.

A member that declares itself **dormant** (`"dormant": true` in its own declaration) is out of the
freshness sweep and out of the usage denominator — its scheduler is stopped, so its mount falls
behind by design and its silence says nothing about any skill. It stays a **member**: membership
is unchanged, because dormancy is about upkeep, not membership.

**Every report enumerates the full fleet.** Whatever a repo's state — covered, dormant, uncovered,
excluded, archived, a fork, inactive today, or simply not measured by that sweep — each sweep's
report names it under exactly one state rather than dropping it. A roster that names only the
exceptions has silent holes, and a reader cannot tell "fine" from "fell out of the report": the
census lists covered members (dormant ones flagged) alongside the uncovered; the freshness sweep
names its fresh members and its out-of-scope repos with why; the usage sweep's `coverage` section
accounts for every repo under the owner and its run report flags folding members with no captured
activity that day; force-baseline reports every repo it did *not* dispatch, with the reason.

The fourth is not a sweep and not a task: **force-baseline** answers no recurring question, so it has
no cadence to schedule. It is the owner pressing *Run workflow* — fire every member's own scheduler
with `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` so the fleet picks canon up now instead of over the next day. It takes a
repo filter, a dry run, and an opt-in for dormant members; it writes nothing to any member (one queued
Actions run each). It then **follows** what it fired — a `204` is *queued*, not baselined — until every
member has finished baselining, agentic handoffs included, and reports what the fleet did: which members
moved and from which canon ref to which, lines changed, per-member timing, errors and warnings, whether
an agent ran. A dry run prints the same report with true zeros, so its shape can be inspected without
changing anything. Its `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow adds no cron, so the
vendored scheduler stays the enforcer's only one — and because GitHub reads workflows solely from a
repo's own `.github/`, the [`sheepdog-fleet-baseline`](../../migrations/active_migrations/2026-08-05-sheepdog-fleet-baseline.mjs)
migration keeps a byte-identical copy there, gated on the repo declaring this pack. The nightly's own
token cannot write a workflow file, so the converge withholds it and baselining's agent stage lands it
over MCP ([#649](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/649)) — automatic either way.

Each sweep lives **inside its task's folder**, because nothing outside that task uses it; force-baseline
lives in [fleet-baseline/](fleet-baseline/) beside them, because it belongs to no task. Only what they
all share sits at the pack root: [fleet-api.mjs](fleet-api.mjs) (the cross-repo REST primitives) and
[fleet-config.mjs](fleet-config.mjs) (the one reader of this pack's entry `config`).

The rest of the machinery — running the daily-run, the task engine (`engine/scheduler/`), scheduling —
is Claudinite **core**. Carries no conformance checks. Policy + config: [RULES.md](RULES.md).

# Fleet fit — adopt the packs a member's shape suspects

Two stages. The first is [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) → the sweep ([`check-fleet-fit.mjs`](check-fleet-fit.mjs)), which runs as `prework` before you start: it enumerates the fleet, runs every canon pack's fingerprint against every covered member, and converges one `fleet-fit` issue per member in **this** (sheepdog) repo. By the time you read this, that has already happened.

**You are the second stage.** Your job is to turn accepted suspicions into reviewed PRs on the members, and the whole of *how* is the [adopt-pack](../../../grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-pack/SKILL.md) skill — including what to do about failing checks and unanswered interview questions, which that skill defines for unattended runs like this one. Don't re-derive it here.

## 1. Read the work list

The open issues labelled `fleet-fit` in this repo. Each names one member and the packs its shape fingerprints but its declaration does not carry. There is no work list anywhere else — no branch, no file, nothing threaded into your dispatch issue. **If no fit issue is open, there is nothing to do: say so and stop.** That is the ordinary outcome on a fleet that is already declaring what it should.

Take them **oldest first**, and take as many as you can finish properly. One member fully adopted beats four half-adopted: a member you started and abandoned mid-adoption is worse than one you never touched, because its declaration now names packs whose content was never vendored.

## 2. Confirm the suspicion before acting on it

A fingerprint **suspects**; it does not prove. This is the same judgment the retired `pack-declaration` check was deleted for making automatically (`engine/checks/README.md`) — so make it deliberately, per pack:

- Read that pack's `README.md` and its `ruleRoutingGuidance`. Does the member's actual use match what the pack owns, or did the marker merely happen to be present? A `package.json` in a repo that ships no JavaScript is a fixture, not a Node project.
- Where the issue lists packs under **Not decided from outside**, you can settle them exactly — you have the member checked out, which the sweep did not. Use `localFits` from `engine/checks/fingerprint-fit.mjs` against a context built over that checkout; it decides every fingerprint the REST sweep had to defer.
- A pack you judge **not** wanted is a real answer. Say which and why in a comment on the fit issue, and don't declare it. If every pack on the issue is declined, close it `not planned` — the sweep honours a deliberate `not_planned` close and will not reopen it.

## 3. Adopt, per member

For each member with at least one confirmed pack, run **adopt-pack** against that repo with the confirmed packs. It owns declaring, the interview, re-vendoring, scaffolding, getting the checks green, and landing one PR.

Two things belong to you rather than the skill:

- **One PR per member**, not one per pack — a member's adoption is one reviewed change.
- **Link both ways**: the PR body names the `fleet-fit` issue, and you comment the PR link on that issue. The sweep closes the issue on its own once the member's declaration carries the packs; your comment is what makes the intervening week legible.

## 4. Report

Comment on your dispatch issue: per member, the packs adopted with a PR link, the packs declined with the reason, and any member left for a human — an adoption blocked on an interview question is exactly that, and naming it is the whole handoff.

## What you must not do

- **Never merge.** This task is ceilinged at `open-pr` and the executor enforces it in code (`verify-outcome.mjs`); merging fails the run.
- **Never declare a pack you did not confirm**, and never guess an interview answer to get past it — see adopt-pack's rule on that. A declaration nobody chose is the failure mode this whole sweep exists to avoid recreating from the other direction.
- **Never touch a dormant or uncovered member.** The sweep already excluded them; if one is on an issue, that issue is stale — say so rather than acting on it.
- **Never apply `ready-for-agent` or `ready-for-agent-fleet` to a fit issue.** Both labels are scheduler triggers ([scheduled-tasks.md](../../../basics/scheduled-tasks.md)); a fit issue is a work list, not a dispatch.

# (`packs-tests/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs` and so on), so a test at an unlisted depth
        # was silently never run — which is exactly how vendoring/'s two files sat outside
        # CI. `**` removes depth from the question; what remains is the root list, and
        # engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the moment a tracked test lands
        # outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit; adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ + the other top-level canon code (migrations/, …);
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs-tests/             every canon pack's tests, mirroring packs/
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.

          tests=(engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs vendoring/**/*.test.mjs dev/tools/**/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs)

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1
sheepdog: add the weekly fleet-fit sweep, and define unattended adoption

A pack's `detect` fingerprint is consulted exactly once, at bootstrap's
`--init`. Baselining backfills the seeded packs and each declared pack's
`requires` closure but never re-fingerprints, so a member that grows into a
pack after adoption is never told the pack exists — the owner has to already
know what to ask for. The census asks whether a repo is a member; freshness
asks whether that membership still means anything; both take the declared pack
set as given. Nothing asked whether that set still matches the repo.

fleet-fit is that re-ask, weekly, from the outside. Two stages, split where the
work changes kind: an agentless `prework` enumerates the fleet, runs every canon
fingerprint against each covered member's tree over REST, and converges one
`fleet-fit` issue per member; a `sonnet` stage then confirms the suspicion and
runs adopt-pack against the member. Ceilinged at `open-pr` and never
auto-merged, because declaring a pack switches on checks that run in that
member's CI the moment they land.

The split follows the canon's own rule for a cross-repo feature: the per-repo
half is engine/checks/fingerprint-fit.mjs — pack-agnostic, fleet-blind, and the
complete answer when it has a checkout — and the aggregation half lives in
sheepdog, the only place that knows which repos exist.

Two things the sweep refuses to get wrong:

- It fingerprints against a scratch clone of `canonRepo`, not this repo's mount.
  A mount carries only the packs its repo declares (four, for a sheepdog repo),
  so sweeping against it would test every member against almost nothing and
  report the whole fleet as fitted. It refuses a corpus too small to be canon
  and states the denominator in its report.
- A fingerprint it cannot decide is reported undecided, never false. Path-only
  fingerprints resolve from one tree call; content-reading ones resolve from a
  bounded prefetch of exactly the files they asked for; one that greps every
  source file exceeds that budget and is deferred to the agent's checkout. A
  truncated tree listing makes every non-match on that repo undecided too.

A fit finding is a recommendation, never a verdict — the `pack-declaration`
check was deliberately retired because declaring is the project's call, and this
must not re-introduce it one rung out. The issue body says "suspects", and a
`not planned` close is a standing answer the sweep honours.

adopt-pack gains the two rules this task needs and every unattended adoption
does: a failing check is the adopting run's work (never silenced by `rules`/
`accept`, never fixed by undeclaring), and an interview question with nobody
present is a hard stop — finish everything it does not gate, get the tree green,
then hand off in the open rather than guessing an answer nobody gave.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NhhfeihyMZtaBL1CvHWqV8
EOF

input.body:
## The gap

A pack's `detect` fingerprint is consulted **exactly once**, at bootstrap's `--init`. Baselining backfills the seeded packs and each declared pack's `requires` closure, but never re-fingerprints. So a member that grows into a pack after adoption — adds a `package.json`, a `firebase.json`, a Chrome manifest — is never told the pack exists, and the owner has to already know what to ask for.

The census asks *is this repo a member*; freshness asks *is that membership still meaning anything*. Both take the declared pack set as given. Nothing asked whether that set still **matches the repo**.

## The task

`fleet-fit` — weekly, in the sheepdog pack. Two stages, split where the work changes kind:

| stage | what it does |
|---|---|
| `prework` (agentless) | enumerate the fleet, run every canon fingerprint against each covered member's tree over REST, converge one `fleet-fit` issue per member, publish the full roster |
| agent (`sonnet`, `session_scope: fleet`) | confirm the suspicion against a real checkout, then run **adopt-pack** against the member |

`expected_outcome: 'open-pr'` and never `merged-pr`: declaring a pack switches on conformance checks that run in that member's CI from the moment they land, so it is always reviewed.

The split follows the canon's own rule for a cross-repo feature — the per-repo half is `engine/checks/fingerprint-fit.mjs` (pack-agnostic, fleet-blind, and the *complete* answer when it has a checkout); the aggregation half lives in sheepdog, the only place that knows which repos exist.

## Two things it refuses to get wrong

**It fingerprints against canon, not against the enforcer's mount.** A consumer's `.claudinite/shared/` carries the vendor set for the packs *it* declares — four, for a sheepdog repo. Running the fingerprints out of the mount would test every member against a handful of packs and report the whole fleet as perfectly fitted, silently. So the sweep shallow-clones `canonRepo` to scratch, refuses a corpus too small to be canon, and **states the denominator in its report**.

**A fit finding is a recommendation, never a verdict.** The `pack-declaration` conformance check was deliberately retired because declaring a pack is the project's call; this must not re-introduce it one rung further out. The issue body says "suspects", and a `not planned` close is a standing answer the sweep honours rather than reopening weekly.

Two rules this task needs and every unattended adoption does, added to the skill rather than restated in the task brief:

- **A failing check is the adopting run's work**, not the reviewer's — never silenced via `rules`/`accept`, never "fixed" by undeclaring the pack. A finding that genuinely cannot be satisfied is evidence the pack is not the right fit; drop it and let the smaller adoption land.
- **An interview question with nobody present is a hard stop.** Never guess an answer. Finish everything the question does not gate, **get the tree green first**, then hand off in the open — an incomplete adoption in a green repo is a handoff; in a red one it is a bug report.

input.body:
## The gap

A pack's `detect` fingerprint is consulted **exactly once**, at bootstrap's `--init` (`engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`). Baselining backfills the `seededByDefault` packs and each declared pack's `requires` closure, but it never re-fingerprints.

So a repo that grows into a pack *after* adoption — adds a `package.json`, a `firebase.json`, a JWT library, a Chrome manifest — is never told the pack exists. `adopt-pack` is the manual path, and it requires the owner to already know what to ask for.

The existing sweeps don't cover it:

- **fleet-census** stops at the binary — carries a tracked `.claudinite-checks.json`, or doesn't.
- **fleet-freshness** takes the declared pack set as given and asks only whether the vendored mount is stale.
- **growth-discover-packs** runs *inside* each member and does note "should declare canon pack X instead" — but its deliverable is a new *local* pack, that note lands only in a per-repo tracker issue, and a member whose scheduler is dead runs it no more than it runs anything else. Self-maintenance can't detect its own absence; that's the whole reason sheepdog's outside look exists.

## What's wanted

A weekly, fleet-wide outside look: for each covered, non-dormant member, which canon packs does its shape fingerprint that its declaration does not carry — and then act on it via `adopt-pack`.

## Constraints worth stating up front

- **A fit finding is a recommendation, never a verdict.** The `pack-declaration` conformance check was deliberately retired (`engine/checks/README.md`) because declaring a pack is the project's call — "a `marker` is a way to *suspect* a pack is needed, never proof it must be". This must not re-introduce that check one rung further out.
- **Only ~9 of 15 fingerprints are answerable from a path listing.** The rest read file *contents*, and `ctx.read` is synchronous — so a REST-based sweep cannot decide them all. Whatever it cannot decide must be reported as undecided, never as a non-match.
- **The enforcer's own mount is not the canon corpus.** `.claudinite/shared/` carries only the vendor set for the packs that repo declares, so fingerprinting out of the mount would test the fleet against a handful of packs and report everything as fitted, silently.
- Adoption run by an unattended agent needs rules the `adopt-pack` skill doesn't currently state: what to do about failing checks, and what to do when a pack's adoption interview has questions and nobody is present to answer them.

## Owner direction

> Build the task however you see fit. When a pack is deemed relevant - you need to run the adopt pack skill, and if there are failing checks - fix them, and if there are user questions/interviews - stop and don't continue (but fix tests before letting the user answer the questions). Actually - these definitions should be added to the adopt-pack skill in general.

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+// Which executor session a task's dispatch goes to — and whose decision that is.
+//
+// Two executor routines exist: the ordinary one, whose session holds this repo
+// alone, and a broader one whose session holds the owner's repos. Keeping the
+// fleet-wide grant off every project's executor is the whole point of the split, so
+// something has to say which a dispatch belongs to.
+//
+// IT IS THE PACK'S DECISION, NOT THE TASK'S (owner ruling, 2026-08-09). A pack whose
+// entire purpose is reaching other repos gives every task it contributes that reach —
+// the task does not opt into it, and a task author asked to choose can only get it
+// wrong in one of two ways: forget it, and the task runs in a session that cannot see
+// what it was written to read (silently, forever — the executor declines the dispatch
+// and the scheduler re-arms it hourly); declare it where it was not warranted, and an
+// ordinary project's dispatch carries a fleet-wide grant it never needed. Declaring it
+// once, on the pack, makes it a property of the reach rather than a per-task
+// checkbox — and there is exactly one place to look to find out which packs have it.
+//
+// The task-level `session_scope` field is DEPRECATED and still honoured. It is the
+// older spelling of the same fact, it still routes correctly, and nothing that
+// declares it breaks; it is simply no longer where the decision belongs. The
+// `deprecated-session-scope` conformance check (basics) is the migration pressure.
+
+export const SESSION_SCOPES = ['self', 'fleet'];
+export const DEFAULT_SESSION_SCOPE = 'self';
+
+export const isSessionScope = (v) => SESSION_SCOPES.includes(v);
+
+// Resolve the scope for one task, and say WHERE the answer came from — callers
+// report the deprecated path rather than silently accepting it.
+//
+//   { scope, source }  source: 'pack' | 'task (deprecated)' | 'default'
+//
+// The pack wins when it declares `fleet`. That is not an arbitrary precedence: a pack
+// declaring fleet reach is asserting something about every task it contributes, and a
+// task inside it cannot be less-reaching than the executor it is filed to — `self` on
+// such a task would be a narrowing the routing cannot express anyway. A pack that
+// declares nothing (or `self`) leaves the answer to the deprecated task field, which
+// is exactly the compatibility path.
+export function resolveSessionScope({ pack = null, decl = {} } = {}) {
+  if (pack?.sessionScope === 'fleet') return { scope: 'fleet', source: 'pack' };
+  if (isSessionScope(decl?.session_scope)) {
+    return { scope: decl.session_scope, source: 'task (deprecated)' };
+  }
+  return { scope: DEFAULT_SESSION_SCOPE, source: 'default' };
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+import { finding } from '../../engine/checks/helpers/findings.mjs';
+
+// `session_scope` on a task declaration is DEPRECATED (owner ruling, 2026-08-09).
+// Which executor session a dispatch goes to follows from the OWNING PACK's reach —
+// `sessionScope` on the manifest — not from a per-task field.
+//
+// The reason it moved is that a task author choosing it can only get it wrong. Forget
+// it on a task that reaches other repos and the dispatch is filed to the self
+// executor, which declines it as another scope's; the session ends without
+// commenting, the scheduler re-arms the issue hourly, and the task never runs —
+// silently and forever. Declare it where it was not warranted and an ordinary
+// project's dispatch carries a fleet-wide session grant it never needed. Neither
+// mistake is visible in a run report. A pack whose whole purpose is reaching other
+// repos knows the answer once, for everything it contributes.
+//
+// ADVISORY, not blocking, and deliberately so: the field still WORKS
+// (engine/scheduler/session-scope.mjs honours it wherever the pack declares nothing),
+// so a repo carrying one is out of date, not broken. Blocking here would break repos
+// that are running correctly, which is not what a deprecation is for.
+//
+// RELEVANCE FIRST (engine/checks/README.md): keyed off a `tasks/<name>/task.mjs`
+// existing and mentioning the field, so it is inert on every repo without tasks and
+// on every task that already moved.
+const TASK_MJS = /(^|\/)tasks\/[^/]+\/task\.mjs$/;
+// The declaration site, not a mention in a comment — a task file that merely explains
+// where its scope comes from (as sheepdog's fleet-fit does) is the OUTCOME this check
+// wants, and flagging it would punish the migration it is asking for.
+const DECLARES = /^\s*session_scope:\s*['"]/m;
+
+const rule = {
+  id: 'deprecated-session-scope',
+  severity: 'advisory',
+  description: 'A tasks/<name>/task.mjs does not declare session_scope — the executor session scope is the owning pack\'s `sessionScope`, not a per-task field',
+  doc: 'packs/basics/scheduled-tasks.md',
+  why: 'a task author choosing the scope can only get it wrong: forgotten, the dispatch goes to an executor that declines it and the task never runs while the scheduler re-arms it hourly; over-declared, an ordinary project\'s dispatch carries a fleet-wide grant — and neither shows up in a run report',
+
+  run(ctx) {
+    const out = [];
+    for (const file of ctx.files.filter((f) => TASK_MJS.test(f))) {
+      const text = ctx.read(file);
+      if (text === null || !DECLARES.test(text)) continue;
+      out.push(finding(rule, {
+        file,
+        what: 'declares the deprecated task-level "session_scope"',
+        fix: 'drop the field and declare `sessionScope` on the owning pack\'s pack.mjs instead — every task the pack contributes then carries that reach (the field still routes correctly until you do)',
+      }));
+    }
+    return out;
+  },
+};
+
+export default rule;

scheduler: the executor scope is the pack's, deprecate task-level session_scope

A task author choosing which executor session its dispatch goes to can only get
it wrong, and both ways are invisible. Forget `session_scope` on a task that
reaches other repos and the dispatch is filed to the self executor, which
declines it as another scope's — the session stops without commenting, the
scheduler re-arms the issue hourly, and nothing ever runs it. Declare it where
it was not warranted and an ordinary project's dispatch carries a fleet-wide
session grant it never needed. Neither shows up in a run report.

A pack whose whole purpose is reaching other repos knows the answer once, for
everything it contributes. So the scope moves to the pack manifest —
`sessionScope: 'fleet'` — and no task declares one. sheepdog declares it; its
fleet-fit task drops the field it was carrying, and the three agentless sweeps
gain the reach they never needed to state (they dispatch nothing, so it costs
them nothing, and no task file here can forget it).

The task-level field is DEPRECATED, not removed. It still routes correctly
wherever the owning pack declares nothing, so no repo carrying one breaks — the
canon's own canon-curation tasks still run on it. `session-scope.mjs` is the one
resolver both paths go through, and it reports which path answered, so a caller
can name the deprecated one rather than silently accepting it. The task contract
keeps validating the field rather than ignoring it: a deprecated field that
accepts a typo mis-routes to an executor that declines it, which is the same
silent-forever failure this change exists to remove.

`deprecated-session-scope` (basics) is the migration pressure — advisory, because
a repo carrying the old field is out of date rather than broken, and blocking
would break repos that are running correctly. It keys off the declaration site,
not a mention: a task file explaining that its reach comes from its pack is the
outcome being asked for, and flagging it would get the explanation deleted.

One layering note: the scope vocabulary lives with the manifest spec in
pack-schema.mjs, and the scheduler imports it. The reverse broke the pack_loader
fixtures, which build a canon tree with no scheduler in it — a useful proof that
the dependency runs scheduler → pack_loader and not back.

Refs #708

Comment class: process-change (where the executor scope is declared moves from the task to the pack, and the old field is deprecated)

Pushed to **[#707](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/707)**.

**The scope is now the pack's.** `sessionScope: 'fleet'` on `pack.mjs`; sheepdog declares it, `fleet-fit` drops the field it was carrying, and no task decides anything. Resolution runs through one module (`engine/scheduler/session-scope.mjs`), resolved once in `discover.mjs` — the only place holding both the manifest and the declaration — so `run.mjs` routes on `task.sessionScope` and never reads the deprecated field.

Verified end to end:

```
sheepdog/fleet-fit           → fleet (pack)
sheepdog/fleet-census        → fleet (pack)
canon-curation/growth-promote→ fleet (task (deprecated))
basics/baselining            → self  (default)
```

**The old field still works** — the two canon-curation tasks route correctly on it, untouched. `deprecated-session-scope` (basics, **advisory**) is the migration pressure; it fires on exactly those two. Advisory, not blocking, because a repo carrying the field is out of date rather than broken, and blocking would break repos that are running correctly.

Two things worth flagging:

**The contract still validates the deprecated field rather than ignoring it.** A deprecated field that silently swallows a typo mis-routes the dispatch to an executor that declines it — the same silent-forever failure the move exists to remove. So a bad value is still a loud contract error; the fix text now points at the pack.

**The check keys off the declaration site, not a mention.** `fleet-fit`'s task file explains *where its reach comes from* — that's the outcome being asked for, and a looser regex would have flagged it and got the explanation deleted. There's a test pinning that, and I confirmed it fails when the regex is loosened.

One layering discovery: putting the scope vocabulary in the scheduler and importing it from `pack-schema.mjs` broke 11 pack_loader tests — their fixtures build a canon tree with no scheduler in it. That's a real proof the dependency runs scheduler → pack_loader and not back, so the vocabulary lives with the manifest spec now.

Verification: **1346 tests, 0 failures**; **0 blocking**, 19 advisory (17 pre-existing + the 2 intended deprecation findings); vendor closure clean for `basics` alone and `basics+sheepdog`; catalog tally updated 79 → 80.

> ⚠️ Still open: **[#707](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/707) awaits your review** (both commits, tracked by [#708](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/708)). The two `canon-curation` tasks are deliberately left on the deprecated field — say the word if you'd rather I migrate them and clear the advisories.

content.text:
Fixed — and the check was right to stop me.

**Chose the fixture, not a migration record.** The change is additive: `sessionScope` is a new optional manifest field, nothing needs moving across, and a record would claim otherwise. The guidance says the fixture is the honest answer in exactly that case.

**The `legacy-task` shape** is what a member looks like right now — a local pack declaring no `sessionScope`, whose scheduled task still carries the deprecated `session_scope`. That's every un-migrated consumer in the fleet.

I checked it actually holds the line rather than just passing, by breaking the change two ways:

| break | result |
|---|---|
| make `sessionScope` **required** on the manifest | 13 of 14 rehearsals red |
| raise `deprecated-session-scope` to **blocking** | `legacy-task` red in both modes |

Both are the ways a member that hasn't migrated would stop converging, and the fixture catches both.

One thing I found and wrote into the fixture rather than letting it pass as implied coverage: the rehearsal runs the vendor and the sweeps, **never the scheduler** — so it cannot prove the deprecated field still *routes* to `fleet`. I confirmed that by breaking the contract validation and watching the rehearsal stay green. That claim belongs to `engine-tests/scheduler/session-scope.test.mjs`, and the fixture comment now says so instead of overclaiming.

Verification: **1348 tests, 0 failures**; 0 blocking, 19 advisory (17 pre-existing + the 2 intended deprecation findings).

> ⚠️ Still open: **[#707](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/707) awaits your review** — three commits now (fleet-fit, the scope deprecation, this fixture), tracked by [#708](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/708).

Comment class: correction (my `sessionScope: 'fleet'` invention answered a question nobody was asking) + process-change (session scope retired to one sanctioned holdout)

You're right, and the question answers itself: **it helped nobody.** The label split exists to keep the fleet-wide grant off an executor that *doesn't* hold the fleet. The sheepdog repo's executor *does* hold it — that repo is the enforcer; declaring the pack is the statement of reach. Routing its own dispatches to a second label inside the same repo was ceremony. Pushed to [#707](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/707).

**Gone:** the pack-level `sessionScope` manifest field (never reached a consumer — it existed only on this branch), the resolver module, the resolution step in `discover.mjs`, and any scope on sheepdog. `fleet-fit` now dispatches to plain `ready-for-agent`:

```
sheepdog/fleet-fit           → ready-for-agent
canon-curation/growth-promote        → ready-for-agent-fleet
canon-curation/growth-discover-packs → ready-for-agent-fleet
everything else              → ready-for-agent
```

**The one good reason, used once:** you named `growth-promote` as the exception, but `growth-discover-packs` (the canon-curation fleet sweep, not its per-repo namesake) is the identical shape — it reads every member's tree from the canon repo, whose ordinary executor is the *one* executor that genuinely doesn't hold the fleet. Dropping its field would strand its dispatches with an executor that declines them, silently and forever. So both canon-curation tasks keep the deprecated field; everything else lost it.

**Still standing:** the field validates and routes while it lingers (a typo is still rejected loudly), the advisory `deprecated-session-scope` check now names the curation tasks as the sanctioned holdout — its two findings on those files are the record of the exception, not drift — and the rehearsal `legacy-task` fixture holds the retirement harmless to any consumer still carrying the field.

Verification: 1345 tests green, 0 blocking / 19 advisory (same 17 + the 2 sanctioned), routing verified end-to-end above.

> ⚠️ Still open: **[#707](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/707) awaits your review** — four commits, tracked by [#708](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/708). If you'd rather `growth-discover-packs` lose the field too and move to some other mechanism, say so — but as-is it would break it.

2	
3	Two stages. The first is [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) → the sweep ([`check-fleet-fit.mjs`](check-fleet-fit.mjs)), which runs as `prework` before you start: it enumerates the fleet, runs every canon pack's fingerprint against every covered member, and converges one `fleet-fit` issue per member in **this** (sheepdog) repo. By the time you read this, that has already happened.
4	
5	**You are the second stage.** Your job is to turn accepted suspicions into reviewed PRs on the members, and the whole of *how* is the [adopt-pack](../../../grow_with_claudinite/skills/adopt-pack/SKILL.md) skill — including what to do about failing checks and unanswered interview questions, which that skill defines for unattended runs like this one. Don't re-derive it here.
6	
7	## 1. Read the work list
8	
9	The open issues labelled `fleet-fit` in this repo. Each names one member and the packs its shape fingerprints but its declaration does not carry. There is no work list anywhere else — no branch, no file, nothing threaded into your dispatch issue.
10	
11	The list is often **empty**, and an empty list is a complete run with an empty outcome — a fleet already declaring what it should. Report it as that, in the words the sweep used: no member carries an undeclared fit this week.
12	
13	Take them **oldest first**, and take as many as you can finish properly. One member fully adopted beats four half-adopted: a member you started and abandoned mid-adoption is worse than one you never touched, because its declaration now names packs whose content was never vendored.
14	
15	## 2. Confirm the suspicion before acting on it
16	
17	A fingerprint **suspects**; it does not prove. This is the same judgment the retired `pack-declaration` check was deleted for making automatically (`engine/checks/README.md`) — so make it deliberately, per pack:
18	
19	- Read that pack's `README.md` and its `ruleRoutingGuidance`. Does the member's actual use match what the pack owns, or did the marker merely happen to be present? A `package.json` in a repo that ships no JavaScript is a fixture, not a Node project.
20	- Where the issue lists packs under **Not decided from outside**, you can settle them exactly — you have the member checked out, which the sweep did not. Use `localFits` from this task's own [`fingerprint-fit.mjs`](fingerprint-fit.mjs) against a context built over that checkout; it decides every fingerprint the REST sweep had to defer.
21	- A pack you judge **not** wanted is a real answer. Say which and why in a comment on the fit issue, and don't declare it. If every pack on the issue is declined, close it `not planned` — the sweep honours a deliberate `not_planned` close and will not reopen it.
22	
23	## 3. Adopt, per member
24	
25	For each member with at least one confirmed pack, run **adopt-pack** against that repo with the confirmed packs. It owns declaring, the interview, re-vendoring, scaffolding, getting the checks green, and landing one PR.
26	
27	Two things belong to you rather than the skill:
28	
29	- **One PR per member**, not one per pack — a member's adoption is one reviewed change.
30	- **Link both ways**: the PR body names the `fleet-fit` issue, and you comment the PR link on that issue. The sweep closes the issue on its own once the member's declaration carries the packs; your comment is what makes the intervening week legible.
31	
32	## 4. Report
33	
34	Comment on your dispatch issue: per member, the packs adopted with a PR link, the packs declined with the reason, and any member left for a human — an adoption blocked on an interview question is exactly that, and naming it is the whole handoff.
35	
36	## What you must not do
37	
38	- **Never merge.** This task is ceilinged at `open-pr` and the executor enforces it in code (`verify-outcome.mjs`); merging fails the run.
39	- **Never declare a pack you did not confirm**, and never guess an interview answer to get past it — see adopt-pack's rule on that. A declaration nobody chose is the failure mode this whole sweep exists to avoid recreating from the other direction.
40	- **Never touch a dormant or uncovered member.** The sweep already excluded them; if one is on an issue, that issue is stale — say so rather than acting on it.
41	- **Never apply `ready-for-agent` or `ready-for-agent-fleet` to a fit issue.** Both labels are scheduler triggers ([scheduled-tasks.md](../../../basics/scheduled-tasks.md)); a fit issue is a work list, not a dispatch.

1	// sheepdog task: fleet-fit — does each covered member declare the packs its SHAPE
2	// suspects? The fourth fleet question, and the first one with an agent stage.
3	//
4	// WHY: a pack's `detect` fingerprint is consulted exactly ONCE, at bootstrap's
5	// `--init`. Baselining backfills the seeded packs and each declared pack's `requires`
6	// closure; it never re-fingerprints. So a member that grows into a pack after
7	// adoption — adds a package.json, a firebase.json, a Chrome manifest — is never told
8	// the pack exists, and the owner has to already know what to ask for. The census asks
9	// "is this repo a member"; freshness asks "is that membership still meaning
10	// anything"; both take the declared pack set as given. This asks whether that set
11	// still matches the repo.
12	//
13	// TWO STAGES, and the split is the point:
14	//   prework (deterministic, no agent) — enumerate the fleet over the PAT, run every
15	//     canon fingerprint against every covered member's tree, converge one `fleet-fit`
16	//     issue per member with undeclared fits, publish the full roster.
17	//   agent (sonnet) — take the accepted suspicions and ACT on them: adopt-pack against
18	//     the member, per task.md.
19	// Everything decidable in code stays in code; the agent is reached only for the part
20	// that is a judgment and a repo edit.
21	//
22	// WHY sonnet and not opus: the detecting is done by the time the agent starts — the
23	// fingerprint found the shape, the pack's own README states its boundary, and
24	// adopt-pack is an existing procedure with an existing checklist. This applies a pack;
25	// it does not author one (which is why growth-discover-packs is opus). The judgment
26	// left is "is this fingerprint's suspicion actually right for this repo", which is
27	// bounded and, being ceilinged at `open-pr`, always lands in front of a reviewer.
28	//
29	// WHY expected_outcome: 'open-pr' and never merged-pr: declaring a pack turns on
30	// conformance checks that run in that member's CI and at every Stop from the moment
31	// they land. A wrong or over-eager declaration therefore breaks a repo with nobody
32	// having looked — the same reason growth-discover-packs and prose-to-checks-sweep are
33	// reviewed. The ceiling is enforced in code (verify-outcome.mjs), so this line is
34	// what actually keeps auto-merge off the PR.
35	//
36	// WHERE THE FLEET REACH COMES FROM: the repo, not any declaration. The agent works
37	// in MEMBER checkouts, and the enforcer repo's executor session is provisioned with
38	// the owner's repos — declaring the sheepdog pack IS the statement that this repo
39	// reaches the fleet, so the dispatch rides the ordinary `ready-for-agent` label like
40	// every other task's. There is no `session_scope` here and none is wanted: that
41	// field is deprecated (owner ruling, 2026-08-09; the canon's curation tasks are its
42	// one standing use), because the executor's access comes from how the repo is
43	// provisioned, never from what a task asks for.
44	//
45	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
46	
47	export default {
48	  id: 'fleet-fit',
49	  frequency: 'weekly',                   // a repo's shape is slow-moving — the same cadence growth-discover-packs uses for the same reason
50	  precondition_signals: [],              // no signal — every input is another repo's tree, which no per-repo collector can see
51	  agent_model: 'sonnet',                 // applies an existing pack by an existing skill; the detecting already happened in prework
52	  expected_outcome: 'open-pr',           // a new pack ships checks that run in the member's CI — always reviewed, never auto-merged
53	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
54	  prework: 'node worker.mjs',
55	  // One tree listing per member plus a bounded handful of content reads per
56	  // content-reading fingerprint, all serial, with a secondary rate limit on top. The
57	  // same 900s the census and freshness sweeps carry, for the same reason: ~10x the
58	  // expected walk while staying well inside the hourly cadence.
59	  prework_timeout: 900,
60	  // Adopting a pack into a member is a checkout, an interview, a re-vendor, a
61	  // scaffold and a PR — per member with findings. Generous, because it is a runaway
62	  // bound and not a scheduling knob.
63	  agent_execution_timeout: 3600,
64	  required_secrets: ['FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN'], // the account-spanning PAT the sweep reads the fleet with
65	
66	  // Fire weekly unconditionally. Every input lives OUTSIDE this repo — another
67	  // member's tree, another member's declaration — and no per-repo collector can see
68	  // any of them, so there is no signal that would tell us in advance whether the
69	  // answer changed. Cheap to no-op: a fleet that declares what it should opens and
70	  // closes nothing, and the agent stage finds no open fit issue and stops.
71	  precondition() {
72	    return { run: true, reason: 'weekly fleet pack-fit sweep (no-ops cheaply on a fleet whose members already declare what their shape suspects)' };
73	  },
74	};

description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---


The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later, in the conversation half of the repo's scheduled `growth-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.

1	// sheepdog task: fleet-fit — does each covered member declare the packs its SHAPE
2	// suspects? The fourth fleet question, and the first one with an agent stage.
3	//
4	// WHY: a pack's `detect` fingerprint is consulted exactly ONCE, at bootstrap's
5	// `--init`. Baselining backfills the seeded packs and each declared pack's `requires`
6	// closure; it never re-fingerprints. So a member that grows into a pack after
7	// adoption — adds a package.json, a firebase.json, a Chrome manifest — is never told
8	// the pack exists, and the owner has to already know what to ask for. The census asks
9	// "is this repo a member"; freshness asks "is that membership still meaning
10	// anything"; both take the declared pack set as given. This asks whether that set
11	// still matches the repo.
12	//
13	// TWO STAGES, and the split is the point:
14	//   prework (deterministic, no agent) — enumerate the fleet over the PAT, run every
15	//     canon fingerprint against every covered member's tree, converge one `fleet-fit`
16	//     issue per member with undeclared fits, publish the full roster.
17	//   agent (sonnet) — take the accepted suspicions and ACT on them: adopt-pack against
18	//     the member, per task.md.
19	// Everything decidable in code stays in code; the agent is reached only for the part
20	// that is a judgment and a repo edit.
21	//
22	// WHY sonnet and not opus: the detecting is done by the time the agent starts — the
23	// fingerprint found the shape, the pack's own README states its boundary, and
24	// adopt-pack is an existing procedure with an existing checklist. This applies a pack;
25	// it does not author one (which is why growth-discover-packs is opus). The judgment
26	// left is "is this fingerprint's suspicion actually right for this repo", which is
27	// bounded and, being ceilinged at `open-pr`, always lands in front of a reviewer.
28	//
29	// WHY expected_outcome: 'open-pr' and never merged-pr: declaring a pack turns on
30	// conformance checks that run in that member's CI and at every Stop from the moment
31	// they land. A wrong or over-eager declaration therefore breaks a repo with nobody
32	// having looked — the same reason growth-discover-packs and prose-to-checks-sweep are
33	// reviewed. The ceiling is enforced in code (verify-outcome.mjs), so this line is
34	// what actually keeps auto-merge off the PR.
35	//
36	// WHERE THE FLEET REACH COMES FROM: the repo, not any declaration. The agent works
37	// in MEMBER checkouts, and the enforcer repo's executor session is provisioned with
38	// the owner's repos — declaring the sheepdog pack IS the statement that this repo
39	// reaches the fleet, so the dispatch rides the ordinary `ready-for-agent` label like
40	// every other task's. There is no `session_scope` here and none is wanted: that
41	// field is deprecated (owner ruling, 2026-08-09; the canon's curation tasks are its
42	// one standing use), because the executor's access comes from how the repo is
43	// provisioned, never from what a task asks for.
44	//
45	// Self-contained (imports nothing): the whole contract is this default export.
46	
47	export default {
48	  id: 'fleet-fit',
49	  frequency: 'weekly',                   // a repo's shape is slow-moving — the same cadence growth-discover-packs uses for the same reason
50	  precondition_signals: [],              // no signal — every input is another repo's tree, which no per-repo collector can see
51	  agent_model: 'sonnet',                 // applies an existing pack by an existing skill; the detecting already happened in prework
52	  expected_outcome: 'open-pr',           // a new pack ships checks that run in the member's CI — always reviewed, never auto-merged
53	  agent_instructions: 'task.md',
54	  prework: 'node worker.mjs',
55	  // One tree listing per member plus a bounded handful of content reads per
56	  // content-reading fingerprint, all serial, with a secondary rate limit on top. The
57	  // same 900s the census and freshness sweeps carry, for the same reason: ~10x the
58	  // expected walk while staying well inside the hourly cadence.
59	  prework_timeout: 900,
60	  // Adopting a pack into a member is a checkout, an interview, a re-vendor, a
61	  // scaffold and a PR — per member with findings. Generous, because it is a runaway
62	  // bound and not a scheduling knob.
63	  agent_execution_timeout: 3600,
64	  required_secrets: ['FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN'], // the account-spanning PAT the sweep reads the fleet with
65	
66	  // Fire weekly unconditionally. Every input lives OUTSIDE this repo — another
67	  // member's tree, another member's declaration — and no per-repo collector can see
68	  // any of them, so there is no signal that would tell us in advance whether the
69	  // answer changed. Cheap to no-op: a fleet that declares what it should opens and
70	  // closes nothing, and the agent stage finds no open fit issue and stops.
71	  precondition() {
72	    return { run: true, reason: 'weekly fleet pack-fit sweep (no-ops cheaply on a fleet whose members already declare what their shape suspects)' };
73	  },
74	};

A bespoke conformance check per code deprecation doesn't scale — every retired
field would grow its own rule module, test file, and catalog row, all to say
what a standard @deprecated tag says in one line (owner ruling, 2026-08-09).

The deprecated-session-scope check and its test are deleted, and the deprecation
now rides the standard mechanism: an @deprecated JSDoc tag on the contract's
session_scope section (engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs), where linters and
readers alike find it. The two sanctioned holdouts — the canon's curation
tasks, whose dispatches must reach the separate fleet executor because the
canon's ordinary routine does not hold the fleet — each pacify the warning with
a comment at their declaration site saying exactly why they keep the field.

Unchanged, deliberately: the contract still validates a lingering field (a typo
would strand the dispatch with an executor that declines it), the routing still
honours it, and the rehearsal legacy-task fixture still holds the retirement
harmless to an un-migrated consumer. Check tally 80 -> 79.

A bespoke conformance check per code deprecation doesn't scale — every retired
field would grow its own rule module, test file, and catalog row, all to say
what a standard @deprecated tag says in one line (owner ruling, 2026-08-09).

The deprecated-session-scope check and its test are deleted, and the deprecation
now rides the standard mechanism: an @deprecated JSDoc tag on the contract's
session_scope section (engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs), where linters and
readers alike find it. The two sanctioned holdouts — the canon's curation
tasks, whose dispatches must reach the separate fleet executor because the
canon's ordinary routine does not hold the fleet — each pacify the warning with
a comment at their declaration site saying exactly why they keep the field.

Unchanged, deliberately: the contract still validates a lingering field (a typo
would strand the dispatch with an executor that declines it), the routing still
honours it, and the rehearsal legacy-task fixture still holds the retirement
harmless to an un-migrated consumer. Check tally 80 -> 79.

4	---
5	
6	Adding a pack to a repo that already runs Claudinite. Whole-repo bootstrap and the on-demand
7	refresh are [adopt-claudinite](../adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md); this is the narrower act of turning
8	one or more packs on. The declaration is authoritative — declaring is the project's call — so the
9	work is: declare, answer what the pack asks, materialize its content, satisfy what it now demands.
10	
11	## 1. Declare
12	
13	The full directory of adoptable packs — every canon pack with what it covers, how it activates,
14	and what it requires — is vendored in the mount at `.claudinite/shared/packs/directory.GENERATED.md`
15	(canon-side: `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`); read it when choosing, or when the owner asks what
16	could be added.
17	
18	Add each chosen pack's id to `packs` in `.claudinite-checks.json`. A pack that only makes sense
19	alongside another names it in `requires`; `resolveDeclaredPacks` pulls that closure in when the
20	declaration is written, so you declare what you *chose* and its dependencies follow (e.g.
21	`spec-driven-product` pulls `executable-requirements`). An unknown pack name — or an unknown
22	property on an entry — is a blocking **settings** error, not a conformance finding; fix the name.
23	
24	## 2. Interview — the part that is easy to skip and must not be
25	
26	A pack that needs the project's intent before it can provide value declares `questions` on its
27	manifest (see [packs/README.md](../../../README.md) and the machinery in
28	[../adopt-claudinite/interview.mjs](../adopt-claudinite/interview.mjs)). For **every** newly
29	declared pack that asks questions:
30	
31	- Where a question says the repo may already hold the answer (a product brief, an existing
32	  requirements doc, the issue tracker), **read that first and confirm** rather than asking cold.
33	- Otherwise ask the owner directly (`AskUserQuestion`), one question at a time, at the point of
34	  adoption — when a human asked for the adoption, they are present by construction.
35	- Record each answer **verbatim** on that pack's entry as `answers: { "<question-id>": "<text>" }`.
36	  `"n/a — none wanted"` is a valid answer and stops the asking. Where the question carries a
37	  `distill` note, derive the entry's `config` from the answer (e.g. `executable-requirements`'s
38	  spec path → `config.spec`).
39	
40	### When nobody is there to ask
41	
42	Adoption also runs **unattended** — a scheduled task acting on a recommendation, the fleet-fit
43	sweep's agent stage, any run with no human in the loop. The interview is then the hard stop, and
44	the order matters:
45	
46	1. **Never guess an answer, and never leave the question unrecorded.** A pack whose question is
47	   answered by inference carries a decision nobody made, in a file that then propagates by
48	   `requires` closure and outlives whoever could have corrected it. `"n/a"` is an *owner's* answer,
49	   not a default you may write on their behalf.
50	2. **Finish everything the question does not gate, first** — declare, re-vendor, refresh the badge
51	   row, scaffold, and get the checks green (§4, §5). Stopping at the question with a red repo hands
52	   the owner a broken tree *and* a question; stopping with a green one hands them only the question.
53	3. **Then stop, and hand off in the open.** Open the PR with what is settled, name each unanswered
54	   question in the PR body under a heading that says the adoption is incomplete, and say the same
55	   on whatever issue prompted the run. Do **not** merge, do not proceed to a next pack's interview,
56	   and do not re-run the adoption on a later firing hoping the answer appeared — an unanswered
57	   question is a human's, and re-asking it weekly is nagging.
58	
59	A pack that asks nothing adopts fully unattended; this section costs it nothing.
60	
61	## 3. Re-vendor
62	
63	The new packs' prose, checks, and skills must land under the tracked `.claudinite/shared/` mount.
64	Fetch a fresh canon to scratch and run its `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs --target . --ref <sha>`
65	against the checkout — the same whole-set convergence the on-demand refresh uses (adopt-claudinite,
66	[bootstrap.md](../../../../bootstrap.md) Parts 1 and 4). It rebuilds `shared/` from the new vendor
67	set and advances the stamp; sessions never fetch.
68	
69	Then **refresh the README pack-badge row**, from the mount you just rebuilt:
70	
71	```
72	node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs <owner/repo> --badges
73	```
74	
75	Declaring a pack is what makes that row wrong, and adoption is the only moment anything derives it —
76	the nightly deliberately leaves a repo's README alone, so a row not refreshed here stays stale until
77	someone notices by eye. The converge rewrites the row in place between its
78	`<!-- claudinite:packs -->` markers, keeping whatever the repo wrote after the closing one, and is a
79	no-op when the row is already right. A repo that has deleted its row keeps it deleted only if you
80	skip this — dropping the row is a real choice, so don't re-seed one the repo removed on purpose.
81	
82	## 4. Scaffold what the pack now demands
83	
84	A newly active pack may require structure the repo doesn't have yet — deliberately, so the
85	declaration is a statement of intent that its own findings then guide you to satisfy. Run the
86	world sweep and let each finding name the file: e.g. `product-wiki` wants its index and the
87	reviewed `product-requirements/` sink before the isolation wall has anything to guard. Scaffold
88	per the pack's own README template; the pack's rules are the checklist.
89	
90	## 5. Land
91	
92	World and work checks green (`.claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs`; the Stop hook
93	carries the work checks). Commit referencing the task's issue, push, open one PR. Content a pack
94	seeds through this flow — a `product-wiki` wiki's first researched, cited pages — rides the same
95	review gate as any other change; it is never pushed straight to the default branch.
96	
97	**A failing check is your work, not the reviewer's.** Declaring a pack is what switched those rules
98	on, so every finding they now produce belongs to this change — fix it here, in the repo, before the
99	PR opens. Two things that are *not* fixes: silencing a rule by adding it to `rules`/`accept` in
100	`.claudinite-checks.json`, and undeclaring the pack to make the findings stop. Both turn a real
101	signal off on the repo's first exposure to it. If a finding genuinely cannot be satisfied — the pack
102	demands structure this repo has decided against — that is evidence the pack is **not** the right fit:
103	drop it from the declaration, say why on the PR, and let the smaller adoption land.
104	
105	**Never leave the repo red.** Whatever stops you — a check you cannot satisfy, an unanswered
106	interview question, a scaffold that needs a decision — get the tree green first and open the PR on
107	what is settled. An incomplete adoption in a green repo is a handoff; an incomplete adoption in a
108	red one is a bug report against you.

# Fleet pack seeds — does every member declare what this fleet standardizes on?

**This task runs no agent.** It is `agent_model: none` with `prework: node worker.mjs`, so the whole pass is the deterministic [`worker.mjs`](worker.mjs) the scheduler runs as a subprocess, which calls its sibling in this folder, the sweep ([`check-fleet-pack-seeds.mjs`](check-fleet-pack-seeds.mjs)). This file is the human-facing record of what that worker does; there is no dispatch issue and no subagent.

## Why it exists

Some packs need a parameter **no member can derive**, because the answer is a fact about the *fleet* rather than about that repo — where its people's files live, which repo holds something shared, what the group calls itself.

Canon cannot supply it: a bootstrap run does not know **which fleet** it is bootstrapping into, and one fleet's value hardcoded in shared code is exactly the coupling packs exist to prevent. The enforcer can — it *is* the fleet. So this repo's sheepdog entry lists what its members should declare:

```json
{ "id": "sheepdog", "config": { "packSeeds": [ { "id": "<a pack>", "config": { … } } ] } }
```

and the sweep converges that list across every member.

## It names no pack

Every id and every config comes from `packSeeds`. The task and its sweep carry the **mechanism** — "these declarations, in every member" — and the fleet supplies the content. A sweep that named a pack would make the enforcer a second place packs are known, and the next fleet would inherit a choice that was never theirs. A fleet with no `packSeeds` is an ordinary fleet: the sweep says so and stops before walking anything.

a comment at their declaration site saying exactly why they keep the field.

would strand the dispatch with an executor that declines it), the routing still
honours it, and the rehearsal legacy-task fixture still holds the retirement
harmless to an un-migrated consumer. Check tally 80 -> 79.

A bespoke conformance check per code deprecation doesn't scale — every retired
field would grow its own rule module, test file, and catalog row, all to say
what a standard @deprecated tag says in one line (owner ruling, 2026-08-09).

The deprecated-session-scope check and its test are deleted, and the deprecation
now rides the standard mechanism: an @deprecated JSDoc tag on the contract's
session_scope section (engine/scheduler/task-contract.mjs), where linters and
readers alike find it. The two sanctioned holdouts — the canon's curation
tasks, whose dispatches must reach the separate fleet executor because the
canon's ordinary routine does not hold the fleet — each pacify the warning with
a comment at their declaration site saying exactly why they keep the field.

Unchanged, deliberately: the contract still validates a lingering field (a typo
would strand the dispatch with an executor that declines it), the routing still
honours it, and the rehearsal legacy-task fixture still holds the retirement
harmless to an un-migrated consumer. Check tally 80 -> 79.
